subject: How to make a discrete uneven color scale in ggplot2

messages.author: 4072426cef17b1f2
messages.subject: How to make a discrete uneven color scale in ggplot2
parts:
Hi D-RUG,

I have run a whole bunch of linear models and I am plotting the slopes for each of them. The x axis is the number of the regression that I ran and the y axis is the value of the slope that I got for that regression. The color of the point corresponds to the p-value for each of the slopes. I've done this with the following code and attached a picture of what I get.

tplot <- ggplot(bp)
tplot <- tplot + geom_point(aes(x=d, y=b, color=pval)) + geom_hline(aes(yintercept=0)) + xlim(0,367) + labs(x='Day of the Year', y='Slope of Regression Line', title=paste('Minimum Temp Regression Slopes at', name))

As you will notice it is really hard to tell the difference between anything that has a p-value less than 0.25, which is not very helpful. I would like to to have 5 colors, one in each of the following intervals: [0, 0.01], [0.01, 0.05], [0.05, 0.1], [0.1, 0.5], [0.5,1]. I think there might be a way to do this with RColorBrewer, but I am at a loss.

Thanks!
Elise

messages.author: ea15a06de541fa42
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: How to make a discrete uneven color scale in ggplot2
parts:
Hi Elise,

Throw a call to cut(), either in your original dataframe:

bp$pval_bins <- cut(bp$pval, 5)

or in aes(), e.g. color=cut(bp$pval, 5). cut() returns factors with labels that are the intervals. ggplot2 will automatically choose a discrete scale in this case (since these are factors). You can set the bin widths manually — see ?cut for more information.

HTH,
Vince
